subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any schema-valid Gateway WebSocket request carrying `__proto__` or `constructor` data reach a prototype-mutating merge, assignment, or dependency sink that crosses an unauthenticated or scoped security boundary?
rationale: Current source disproves the reported Zod-parser premise but an exhaustive method-specific sink audit or live payload probe is needed before security owners can definitively reject or accept defense-in-depth hardening.

options.title: Request sink-level proof
options.body: Keep the report open briefly for an exact frame, method, downstream sink, and observable prototype mutation, then close as unsupported if none is demonstrated.

options.title: Commission focused audit
options.body: Have a Gateway security owner audit handlers accepting arbitrary nested objects and add a narrow regression probe without changing wire compatibility yet.

options.title: Adopt global filtering
options.body: Reject prototype-related keys during parsing only after assessing compatibility across plugin-defined and forward-compatible payloads.

recommendation.title: Request sink-level proof
recommendation.body: Keep the report open briefly for an exact frame, method, downstream sink, and observable prototype mutation, then close as unsupported if none is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work most directly covers scope, pairing, and requester security boundaries in the active WebSocket handler.
